body: EARLY SYSTEMS CRITIQUE — three implementation-blocking contradictions. (1) The report simultaneously requires separate public/private registrable domains and recommends a one-click flow where the current launcher becomes the fullscreen Stage. If that launcher began on the private origin, its document/SW/storage/session provenance violates the public-byte invariant; cross-origin navigation loses the activation needed for fullscreen. Security wins: either accept the explicit Stage-local fullscreen click, or invert startup so a neutral PUBLIC-domain launcher becomes Stage and opens the private console. Do not promise both two-site isolation and private-launcher one-click. (2) The diagram lets one authoritative Session Service serve private App and public Stage, while the security text says the Audience gateway has no credential/network path to private DB/topic. Split private control authority from a public projection gateway/store; public WSS reads only PublicPresentationState/PublishedDeckArtifact/PublishedAudienceCard. Sanitized display receipts are a separate reverse schema, so call this a content diode, not a literally one-way network. (3) Mirrored pairing is chicken-and-egg: the PC is said to hold only AudienceDisplaySession, yet a pre-existing private console must approve the phone. Safer zero-state flow is inverted: authenticated phone creates/owns session; fresh guest/InPrivate PC opens public Stage and shows a non-authorizing display_join_id; phone scans and approves binding. Pair-before-mirror is acceptable only if the runbook proves the private PC console is gone and the phone heartbeat/controller lease is established before projection begins.
